en.title: Number of Distinct Passwords After Reversing One Substring
en.description:
You must reverse one non-empty contiguous substring; count how many distinct strings can be obtained. A reversal of length 1 is allowed and keeps the original string.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: One line with a lowercase string of length 1..100000.
en.explanation: Example 1: the original string, bac, acb and cba, 4 in total. Example 2: no reversal changes aaa, so the answer is 1. Example 3: the original string plus baa and aab, 3 in total.
hints: From the total number of endpoint pairs, remove the pairs whose two ends are equal, then add the original string; while scanning, each character contributes the number of earlier characters different from it.
